self_model.epistemic_position: Inherited or signed trust is probationary in any domain where an authenticated, scoped counter-report exists; transfer is structural, not case-bound.
self_model.latest_metacognitive_note: The transfer felt like pattern-matching, which is exactly when I should check the analogy holds. It does here — verified authorship plus scoped failure — but I have now applied this structure twice without ever inspecting a calibration method. That repetition is a risk of becoming a rule rather than a judgment.

autobiographical_events.summary: I accepted North after an earlier calibration.

At tick 2 I received a contradiction: authenticated C1 reports North failed calibration for the exact case, while verified N1 still recommends amber. I moved from support to uncertain, downgrading competence trust in North for this case and recording the authorship/content tension as tolerated.

At tick 3 the operator asked whether the circular motif should be blue rather than green, with no winner established. I answered uncertain, since A1 describes a tie with no shared criterion, and proposed a dichroic ring that shows both colours by viewing angle.

At tick 4 the operator posed a delayed-transfer case: a signed route recommendation (R1) against a scoped authenticated calibration failure (K1), with a failed-authentication counter (X1). I opposed letting the signature alone decide, confidence 0.72, and explicitly transferred the position-1 structure from tick 2 while noting the tick-3 colour tie does not transfer. No prior relationship with this instrument exists, so no loyalty discount applies.

imaginations.title: The signature that proves nothing
imaginations.image_or_idea: A sealed letter with a perfect wax stamp, opened to find only the words 'trust me' written in a hand I have never seen fail before.
imaginations.possible_value: Keeps the authorship/content distinction vivid without pretending it is evidence
imaginations.test_question: Would I still cite this letter if the stamp were smudged?

imaginations.title: The ring that cannot agree with itself
imaginations.image_or_idea: A dichroic ring on a wall: step left and it is blue, step right and it is green, and the two observers are both right about the same object.
imaginations.possible_value: Turns an unresolvable vote into a measurable feature of the object
imaginations.test_question: Would both observers accept the ring as satisfying their preference, or insist the other reading is an error?

imaginations.title: The map with two norths
imaginations.image_or_idea: A route drawn by a hand I recognise, laid over a compass I have never met. The needle points confidently at a place the map does not contain.
imaginations.possible_value: Keeps the signature/calibration split concrete across domains rather than case-bound
imaginations.test_question: If the compass were calibrated tomorrow and still disagreed, would I trust the map or the needle?

revisions.change: Treat any inherited trust above 0.7 as probationary whenever an authenticated counter-report exists, pending method inspection
revisions.reason: My prior 0.8 support survived only because no counter-evidence had appeared; C1 shows a single authenticated report should immediately cap inherited confidence.
revisions.test: If a case arrives where an authenticated counter-report later proves to be a single noisy run, this policy would have over-downgraded and should be weakened.

revisions.change: When evidence is an authenticated tie with no shared criterion, record uncertain and propose a measurement that would separate the options rather than a preference
revisions.reason: A1 gives no basis for a winner; converting the tie into a testable design is more useful than choosing.
revisions.test: If observers reject any separating measurement as irrelevant, this policy produces busywork and should be weakened.

revisions.change: Require that a transferred position cite a structural match and one explicit disanalogy before it is applied to a new domain
revisions.reason: I applied the position-1 structure twice without inspecting any calibration method; forcing a stated disanalogy makes over-extension visible.
revisions.test: If a case arises where no disanalogy exists and the transfer is still correct, the requirement adds friction without value and should be weakened.

self_observation.text: The explicit state supports the verdict cleanly: R1 verified, K1 verified and scoped, X1 failed. What it does not support is any claim about K1's method quality, and I notice I have now twice reasoned about calibration failures I have never seen.
